before: @font-face names a font resource that font-family can request. A fallback family remains important while loading or when a resource fails. This tiny original teaching font has only A, B and a space; it is a loading demonstration, not a full reading font or a font-design course.

font-family inside @font-face gives the face its CSS name. src supplies a URL and format hint; url() names the encoded local resource and format("truetype") describes its file format. font-weight and font-style describe which face it is, not an element’s requested appearance. font-display: swap permits fallback text while the face loads. The long data URL is supplied font bytes, not CSS syntax to memorize. The sample rule requests the named face with monospace fallback. Actual loading and glyph width are checked, not merely a family-name string.
Use the supplied original font face for AA with a monospace fallback and swap loading behavior. Keep the supplied encoded resource unchanged.
after: A font controls the shape of letters. A web font is a font the page loads. A fallback font is a backup the browser can use while waiting or if loading fails.

`@font-face` gives a font a name and tells the browser where to load it. The starter already contains a tiny teaching font called Study Stencil. Keep its long encoded file unchanged. It contains only A, B, and a space.
Inside the supplied `@font-face` rule, set `font-display: swap`. This lets the browser show a backup font while the chosen font loads, then switch when it is ready.

before.question: If the named font cannot load, does the fallback name become useless?
choices: The fallback changes the HTML letters.
Yes; all text must disappear forever.
No; the browser can use the fallback family to keep text available.
before.explanation: A font-family list provides alternatives; loading behavior and resource failure must be considered separately from naming a face.

after.question: What can happen if the chosen web font does not load?
choices: The backup changes the letters in the HTML
The words must stay hidden forever
The browser can show the words in the backup font
after.explanation: A backup font helps keep the same words readable if the chosen font cannot load.
